# Results — Study 79 (Sleigh-Ride) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Santa Claus Rally
(Hirsch, *Stock Traders Almanac*): last 5 trading days of the calendar year + first 2
of January. Measured as a mean 7-day window log return vs a random-window baseline and
vs all non-window trading days, on **^GSPC since 1950** (76 windows) and SPY since 1993
(33 windows). As-of **2026-06-12**; Yahoo daily bars with auto-adjusted splits/dividends.
Match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| ^GSPC | 1950-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 19,233 | `0d8c7e7b4944` |
| SPY   | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-12 |  8,400 | `454e519f08e2` |

## The honest test — Santa window vs all other days (^GSPC, 1950-2026)

| Arm | n days | mean (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Santa Claus window** | 537 | **+17.28** | **+4.95** |
| All other trading days (baseline) | 18,695 | +2.77 | +3.92 |
| **Difference (Santa − baseline)** | — | **+14.51** | **+4.16** |

The Santa window mean per day is +17.28 bps vs +2.77 bps for all other days. The HAC
*t*-stat on the difference is **+4.16** — statistically real on the daily-return level.

## Per-window (7-day aggregate) summary

| Tape | n windows | mean (bps) | median (bps) | win-rate | HAC *t* (vs zero) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ^GSPC (1950-2026) | 76 | **+121.5** | +120.4 | **76.3%** | **+4.45** |
| SPY (1993-2026)   | 33 | +77.7 | +79.5 | 69.7% | +2.28 |

The 7-day window averages **+1.2%** on ^GSPC with a 76% win-rate and HAC *t* = 4.45.
On the shorter SPY history (33 windows) the effect is present but weaker (t = 2.28).

## Random-window baseline (null distribution of 7-day returns)

1,000 draws of 7 consecutive trading days from non-year-end dates on ^GSPC:

| | bps |
|---|--:|
| Baseline mean | +17.4 |
| Baseline std | 251.8 |
| Baseline p95 | +378.0 |
| Baseline win-rate | 58.6% |

The Santa mean (+121.5 bps) sits near the **60th percentile** of the random-window
distribution (std 251 bps, p95 = +378 bps) — the effect is real but the per-window
variance is huge. You need 75 years of history to pin down a *t* > 2.

## The 'If Santa Fails, Bears May Come' follow-up claim

Hirsch's follow-up: years when the Santa window was *negative* are predicted to precede
a bad January/Q1. Test: forward 20-trading-day log return after positive vs negative windows.

| Group | n | Forward mean (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|
| After positive Santa window | 58 | +35.0 |
| After negative Santa window | 18 | +183.0 |
| Difference (pos − neg) | — | **−148.0** |
| HAC *t* (pos − neg) | — | **−1.11** |

*If Santa fails, bears come* is **NOT SUPPORTED** on this data: years with a negative
Santa window actually have a *higher* forward mean (+183 bps) than positive-window years
(+35 bps), and the difference t-stat is −1.11 — not statistically significant. The 18
negative-window years show a 67% forward win-rate (vs 62% overall), the *opposite* of
what the myth predicts. Sample size is the main caveat (18 negative-window years).

## Tradability analysis

The Santa window fires **once per year**. At 1 bp round-trip on an S&P 500 ETF:

| Cost | Net 7-day return | Annual contribution |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +121.5 bps | +1.22%/yr |
| 1 bp round-trip | +119.5 bps | +1.20%/yr |

The gross return is real and survives trivial costs because the window fires only once
a year — round-trip cost is ~2 bps vs ~121 bps gross. However:

- The per-window std is **huge** (~251 bps): the trade has a Sharpe of ~0.48 per window.
- The effect is a **calendar overlay** on a buy-and-hold position, not a standalone edge.
  A buy-and-hold investor is already long over this window and receives the return without
  trading. The alpha above that is the +14 bps/day excess — a real but tiny tilt.
- Leverage to make it meaningful requires holding flat outside the window and levering up
  for 7 days/year — which introduces tax drag, management overhead, and timing risk.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** 7-day window mean +121 bps, HAC *t* = 4.45 on ^GSPC (76 years);
  daily diff *t* = 4.16 vs baseline. The effect is statistically real on a long history,
  but the per-window variance is enormous (std 252 bps) and the *SPY-only* history gives
  only *t* = 2.28 (33 windows).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Fires once a year; survives trivial costs; but the ~1.2%/yr
  gross contribution is too small and too volatile to build a standalone strategy.
  Most of the "edge" is just long-equity beta during 7 trading days a year.
- **'If Santa Fails' — NOT SUPPORTED.** The directional forecast for negative windows
  shows the *opposite* sign and *t* = −1.11; insufficient evidence to trade on.
